A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Differential Transformer and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix and figure renumbering; no material comparison gaps were found.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training, scaling, retrieval, hallucination, in-context learning, quantization, ablation, and throughput results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds mathematical-reasoning training and evaluation results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The differential-attention equations, lambda parameterization, headwise normalization, overall architecture, and FlashAttention pseudocode are unchanged. Appendix C applies the retained architectures in additional math-training and evaluation settings.

E1.justification: New Appendix C substantially extends coverage to mathematical reasoning, using synthetic math training data and OpenThoughts-114K-Math distillation data. Evaluation adds GSM-8K, MATH, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, CARP, TABMWP, and CollegeMath, including extended reasoning outputs. Earlier dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The math experiments extend the existing DIFF-versus-Transformer comparison to new tasks. DeepSeek-R1 supplies distillation data; neither it nor o1 is evaluated as an additional competing model.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a substantial two-stage evaluation protocol for the existing 3B models: 20B additional math-training tokens, evaluated every 2B tokens from 6B to 20B, followed by 2B distillation-training tokens and best-checkpoint selection. Output limits are 1K and 16K tokens respectively. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a learning-dynamics analysis: Figure 9 tracks math accuracy across additional training budgets and examines when DIFF's advantage emerges. The original component ablations, attention analysis, quantization tests, and prompt-order robustness analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The prompt-order seed sweeps and best-to-worst range reporting are unchanged, including v1 Figure 9 becoming v2 Figure 11. The added math experiments introduce no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial math results. Figure 9 reports an 11.3-percentage-point final accuracy gap after 20B math-training tokens. Figure 10 reports DIFF versus Transformer averages of 50.8% versus 43.3% after reasoning distillation, with DIFF ahead on all eight benchmarks. Appendix C also reports average reasoning lengths of 6144 versus 6913 tokens. These are new comparisons, while the original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the gradient-flow argument are retained, with Appendix F becoming Appendix G. The added reference to Naderi et al.'s spectral analysis supplies external theoretical context but introduces no new formal statement, derivation, or proof within the paper.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the claimed advantages to include mathematical reasoning. The abstract, conclusion, and central contributions concerning differential attention, noise cancellation, scaling, and context utilization retain their previous scope.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds a cited explanation linking differential attention to balanced attention spectra and resolution of rank collapse. Appendix C interprets the new results as more effective learning of reasoning tasks and evidence that differential attention contributes to mathematical-reasoning performance. Existing interpretations and applicability qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C documents the new training-data sources, the 89K-sample distillation dataset averaging 6K tokens, learning rates of 8e-5 and 1e-5, batch sizes of 4M and 1M tokens, and inherited settings. Existing implementation pseudocode, hardware information, pretraining hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the math benchmarks, synthetic training data, OpenThoughts, o1-style reasoning, and DeepSeek-R1 distillation, plus Naderi et al.'s spectral analysis. These provide focused additional research context; the central positioning of Differential Transformer is retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely preserved. v2 inserts a mathematical-reasoning appendix, updates subsequent appendix references, adds limited introductory and explanatory text and funding acknowledgments, and changes citation and heading styles for the conference format. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the math-training curve in Figure 9 and the benchmark bar chart in Figure 10. The previous appendix robustness figure becomes Figure 11. Existing figures and tables are retained, with limited reflow, heading changes, and conference headers.

improvement.justification: Appendix C provides useful additional evidence that the architecture's benefits extend to mathematical reasoning, using matched training budgets for the two architectures, a learning curve, and results across eight benchmarks. The accompanying training details improve assessability while the original evidence remains intact. This is a bounded improvement: the new experiments report no repeated-run uncertainty and leave the criterion for selecting the best checkpoint unspecified.
